title: Span Cascade Explorer — compact trace mosaic for rapid drilldown
creator: Ava Rodriguez
description:
Goal: Ship a compact, scannable trace drilldown UI that helps engineers discover high-latency spans, correlate by correlation IDs, and pivot quickly to logs, deploy metadata, and cost-per-request overlays.

Problem statement: Current trace drilldown is verbose and requires too much vertical scrolling for long-lived requests. Teams often need to: (1) find the slowest service across many spans, (2) see which correlation IDs touch problematic components, and (3) evaluate token/cost implications for request paths without leaving the trace context.

Proposal: 'Span Cascade Explorer' — a tiled mosaic view that compresses span time into horizontal bands, groups sibling spans into collapsible cascades, and exposes a persistent correlation ribbon for quick filtering. Key features: compact timeline compression, span heatmap (latency + errors), correlation ID strip with hit counts, inline actions (jump to logs, view deployment, open PR linked to service), and a cost overlay toggle that renders estimated token/cost per span and per-path.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype in Figma with desktop & narrow-screen variants, showing collapsed/expanded cascades and hover tooltips with KV cache state.
- Filter bar supports: service, span-kind (client/server), status (error/ok), correlation-id, and custom tag. Filters update both mosaic and correlation ribbon.
- Interaction: clicking a span opens a right-hand details panel; keyboard shortcut 'D' toggles cost overlay; 'C' copies correlation ID.
- Performance: UI renders a 500-span trace with initial layout under 200ms in the mock harness.
- Handoff: deliver tokens, spacing, and component states to engineering with annotated Figma frames and a short prototype recording.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: full replay of request (separate work), span-level step-through animation, and server-side cost calculation (ENG to provide cost hook).
